results.notes: Source variable: 'Topic diversity'; one row per Session/dyad. Treatment is cue, pooling virtual and inperson; control is no cue, pooling the same modalities. Between-dyad design, so round='all' and no first-round or paired result. Published means and SDs: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), Section 5.1.1. Additional exact numerical labels (minimum, median, maximum) in Fig. 5, PDF p. 8 (printed p. 303), also match. They are printed figure labels, not values read from plotted positions. SDs in the reproduced list use denominator G_arm-1 across dyads. The deposited scores are the authors' already scored outcomes; original idea/transcript scoring was not rerun. Analysis uses every nonmissing outcome: 84 dyads. Arm/modality counts: cue/inperson: 20 dyads (40 people); cue/virtual: 21 dyads (42 people); no cue/inperson: 21 dyads (42 people); no cue/virtual: 22 dyads (44 people). Missing outcome rows excluded: ['S5', 'S15']. Rows retained despite missing background covariates: ['S1', 'S2', 'S6', 'S7', 'S9', 'S10', 'S12', 'S17', 'S18', 'S26', 'S29', 'S35']. Section 4.1.1 excludes missing background values specifically from analyses accounting for those factors. The requested unadjusted arm-indicator contrast uses no such factors. The complete-background-covariate alternative has 72 dyads (cue: 34 dyads, mean=2.30365582424, dyad SD=0.285386291924; no cue: 38 dyads, mean=2.08990035742, dyad SD=0.387497563483); it is not the sample used here. No additional exclusions were guessed from the narrative or session number gaps. n_treatment and n_control count people: two partners per observed dyad, as specified in PDF p. 5 (printed p. 300), Section 4.1.1. The overall 86-dyad/172-person roster checks do not establish paper-reported analysis counts, which are absent. The post-surveys contain self-reports only, including a missing Cue response and duplicate participant-ID labels; survey completion is not used as an outcome exclusion or as a participant roster. The posted outcome is jointly produced and scored at dyad level. Arm means are means of shared dyad outcomes, also the participant-weighted means of the shared outcome because every dyad has two people. They do not describe separately scored individual contributions. Participant-level SDs cannot be identified: treatment_sd and control_sd are null, and no dyad rows were duplicated to manufacture individual scores or a participant-level standardizer. The raw difference is treatment minus control in the original dyad-outcome units. difference_se is the OLS intercept-plus-cue slope SE, clustered on Session using CR1 with one observation per randomized dyad: SE^2 = G/(G-2) * [SSE_t/G_t^2 + SSE_c/G_c^2]. n_clusters=G counts all analyzed dyads. This is a new unadjusted contrast, not the paper's REML F test. The REML statistic, denominator degrees of freedom and p value are not claimed as reproduced. The Cue minimum 1.494 printed in Fig. 5a is S9, which has missing dsgn/know, confirming that the published descriptives include background-incomplete dyads despite both candidate samples having the same one-decimal arm summaries.

skipped.reason: No printed arm means, difference, coefficient, numerical test or analyzed arm counts are available in Section 5.1.3 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 304), so the required numerical contrast reproduction cannot be performed. The only numerical idea-count summary is the overall mean 19.4 in Section 5 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 302). The # of all ideas column has 84 observed dyads and mean 19.6785714285714, rounding to 19.7; match=false. Applying complete dsgn/know cases leaves 72 dyads and mean 19.9027777777778, rounding to 19.9, also not 19.4. S5 and S15 have missing idea counts. No further exclusions can be identified from the deposited files without guessing, and no treatment/control contrast or SE was computed for this outcome.

This across-group diversity measure has no participant-level outcome. The deposit contains only dyad aggregates and post-survey responses, not the idea texts, topic assignments, embeddings, centroids or cosine distances used in the analysis. The embedding model is not named, and Section 6.3 (PDF p. 11, printed p. 306) describes a within-condition centroid whereas Appendix A.4.1 (PDF p. 16, printed p. 311) describes an average across groups. The exact procedure cannot be reproduced with the same model and texts. Figure 6 (PDF p. 17, printed p. 312) has no numerical arm summaries or reported Wilcoxon result. No replacement embedding model, inferred figure values or participant-level statistics were used.
